anchors.level_0: No evidence of practical engineering work, internships, co-op programmes, or hands-on laboratory/field experience.
anchors.level_1: Mentions completion of an internship or co-op placement, but roles, tasks, and technical engineering responsibilities are vague or merely listed without context.
anchors.level_2: Clear evidence of an engineering internship, industrial co-op, or substantial hands-on project detailing assigned operational or maintenance duties.
anchors.level_3: Substantial industrial or operating site experience (e.g., refinery, offshore base, manufacturing plant) with specific technical contributions, troubleshooting, and measurable outcomes.

criteria.definition: Measures hands-on application of engineering principles in operational, industrial, or project environments such as plants, offshore sites, or technical co-op placements.
criteria.name: Practical & Field Engineering Exposure

anchors.level_0: No details provided on senior capstone project, technical coursework, or engineering thesis.
anchors.level_1: Lists a senior project title or coursework without describing methodology, personal contribution, or engineering analysis.
anchors.level_2: Presents a well-defined capstone project or thesis with clear problem formulation, relevant engineering methodology, and concrete deliverables.
anchors.level_3: High-impact senior thesis or engineering design project with rigorous modelling, simulation, or physical testing that produced validated results or recommendations.

criteria.definition: Evaluates depth of core engineering knowledge and technical problem-solving demonstrated through senior design projects, capstones, or research theses.
criteria.name: Discipline Engineering Foundation & Capstone

anchors.level_0: No mention of programming, digital tools, process simulation software, or data-driven engineering work.
anchors.level_1: Lists tools or software (e.g., Python, Aspen HYSYS, MATLAB, SQL) as standalone keywords without an example of application.
anchors.level_2: Applies digital or analytical tools within coursework, research, or an internship to model systems, process operational data, or analyse engineering trends.
anchors.level_3: Demonstrates advanced implementation of digital tools or analytics (e.g., automated data pipelines, process optimization models, digital twin components) leading to quantifiable efficiency gains.

criteria.definition: Assesses the ability to apply computational methods, programming languages, process simulation tools, or analytics to solve engineering challenges and enhance efficiency.
criteria.name: Data Analytics & Digital Engineering Tools

anchors.level_0: No awareness or mention of safety principles, hazard identification, or operational compliance.
anchors.level_1: General statements claiming safety consciousness or listing basic safety certifications without practical context.
anchors.level_2: Evidence of working within structured safety frameworks (e.g., laboratory safety officer, hazard assessment/HAZOP coursework, Job Safety Analysis during an internship).
anchors.level_3: Demonstrated proactive safety leadership (e.g., conducted safety audits, authored standard operating procedures, identified near-misses, or implemented hazard mitigation controls in an industrial setting).

criteria.definition: Measures understanding and active adoption of occupational health, process safety systems, hazard identification, and operational compliance required in high-hazard environments.
criteria.name: Process Safety & Risk Management Mindset

anchors.level_0: No demonstration of interest in decarbonisation, emissions reduction, or low-carbon energy solutions.
anchors.level_1: Expresses general interest in sustainability or renewables without supporting coursework, projects, or extracurricular involvement.
anchors.level_2: Active participation in academic electives, student competitions, seminars, or projects addressing decarbonisation, energy efficiency, or clean technology.
anchors.level_3: Significant project, publication, or work contribution specifically tackling energy transition challenges (e.g., carbon capture design, emissions modelling, renewable integration, energy optimisation).

criteria.definition: Evaluates genuine interest and initiative toward low-carbon technologies, emissions reduction, renewable energy, hydrogen, or carbon capture and storage (CCS).
criteria.name: Energy Transition & Decarbonisation Alignment

anchors.level_0: No evidence of collaborative projects, team activities, leadership roles, or technical presentations.
anchors.level_1: Mentions team participation or communication skills without concrete roles, achievements, or context.
anchors.level_2: Documented role in multi-disciplinary team projects, student committee responsibilities, or delivering technical presentations to diverse audiences.
anchors.level_3: Proven leadership in cross-functional engineering teams or student associations, successfully coordinating stakeholders and delivering complex group objectives under deadlines.

criteria.definition: Measures capability to collaborate across multidisciplinary groups, take ownership of shared goals, and communicate complex information effectively in professional settings.
criteria.name: Teamwork, Leadership & Communication

knockouts.description: Candidate must hold or be completing an accredited degree in one of the specified engineering disciplines.
Candidate must graduate or have graduated between 2025 and 2027.
Candidate must be willing to work on rotation at operating sites, including offshore platforms in the Gulf of Thailand.
Candidate must possess lawful right to work in Thailand.

output.role_summary: The Graduate Engineer Programme builds future technical leaders and operations managers across Thara Energy's upstream, downstream, and low-carbon businesses through structured two-year rotations. The ideal candidate pairs a solid discipline-specific engineering foundation with hands-on industrial exposure, proactive safety awareness, analytical capability, and a clear motivation for the energy transition.
